| 1|Acknowledge, and reward, impactful response work at institution, funder, and research community levels |More grant and journal calls focused more on applied analysis, data curation and software than just discovery science. | | 2|Acknowledge, and reward, impactful response work at institution, funder, and research community levels |Committees setting the criteria for doctoral theses and promotion have specifically chosen to exclude response work. | | 4|Acknowledge, and reward, impactful response work at institution, funder, and research community levels |I have moved institution from the one I was at when I was engaged in COVID-19 modeling so I am not sure what progress has happened at this level. I have not noticed obvious changes at funding bodies. UKRI has adopted a changed CV documentation for funding proposals (R4RI) though it is not clear to me how this or whetehr this will impact on what type of work is recognised. | | 5|Acknowledge, and reward, impactful response work at institution, funder, and research community levels |I don't know of specific actions but people recently recruited in academic posts had all played a key role in outbreak response. However they had also published well and been successful in grants. So hard to tell but my feeling is that it is a bit better recognised than a few years ago. I am not confident the trend will continue though. | | 8|Acknowledge, and reward, impactful response work at institution, funder, and research community levels |I don't see any evidence of change taking place in this regard. In fact, since the workshop, I've actually seen more instances of response-driven work being undermined and misunderstood (though acknowledge that this is my own subjective experience and that of my immediate circle). | | 10|Acknowledge, and reward, impactful response work at institution, funder, and research community levels |Clear role of impact in grant application, not only restricted to academic papers. | | 11|Acknowledge, and reward, impactful response work at institution, funder, and research community levels |I have seen some talks by senior academics that might improve awareness by institutional leadership / admin, but that's about the most concrete evidence of anything moving in the direction of practical changes. | | 14|Acknowledge, and reward, impactful response work at institution, funder, and research community levels |I think funders and promotion committees are improving their recognition of all forms of output. | | 1|Ensure response teams are well-staffed, well-resourced, stable, and provided psychological support |There have been funding calls for pandemic training and capacity development on longer timescales. Less progress on long term response positions by default, even at large NGOs. | | 4|Ensure response teams are well-staffed, well-resourced, stable, and provided psychological support |UKRI has put out an epidemic prediciton/prevention funding call though it explicitly does not focus on epidemic management (presumably, if not prevented). The university sector is in general experiencing high funding stress so I expect that ore stable long-term funding opportunities in this sectors have not improved. Many universities have hiring freezes. On an individual level I am aware of a lot of keeness for collaboraiton between academic modelers and UKHSA. We have tried to build this into our funding proposals. I am not sure if there are other formal mechanisms. | | 5|Ensure response teams are well-staffed, well-resourced, stable, and provided psychological support |We are starting to incorporate more training programs and support internally, but we are only at the start. I don't think there has been an improvement unfortunately in terms of sustainable funding, quite the opposite, my feeling is that funders and the public have already lost interest in epidemic preparedness. | | 8|Ensure response teams are well-staffed, well-resourced, stable, and provided psychological support |If anything, I've seen a reduction in the number of long-term (and sufficiently resourced) grants available for response-driven work. I have seen efforts made to improve training and team building outside of response periods and promote inter-agency working (e.g. in CMMID, the new health data science centre). However these are as-hoc examples and I am unsure how widespread or sustained they really are. | | 10|Ensure response teams are well-staffed, well-resourced, stable, and provided psychological support |Training provided for lots of staff, but many staff employed on fixed term contracts due to short term funding restrictions | | 11|Ensure response teams are well-staffed, well-resourced, stable, and provided psychological support |This all seems status quo, including the declining trend in funding prospects that have some stability. | | 14|Ensure response teams are well-staffed, well-resourced, stable, and provided psychological support |None | | 1|Implementing best practices for a sustainable work environment |Increase in RSE roles at UK universities. | | 2|Implementing best practices for a sustainable work environment |Support staff have been made redundant or left. | | 4|Implementing best practices for a sustainable work environment |Again, I have changed institutions over the last few years so it is difficult for me to assess progress over this time period. I do have the impression that continuous review and critique of promotion processes does impove guidance and what is considered, though I have not been on the decision-making side of this. I think that a number of institutions or centres are thinking about how to better onboard new team members so I am optimistic this will improve though I am not sure whetehr it actually has. I think support roles might be inteegrated where research grants/teams are large, which has generally been the case previously. | | 5|Implementing best practices for a sustainable work environment |I have not seen a huge amount of change but we are starting some internal review processes which I hope will improve clarity around criteria for career progress in the near future | | 8|Implementing best practices for a sustainable work environment |The persistent under-resourcing of projects leading to staff who are burnt out and over-worked has only persisted and there continues to be an expectation that staff work unpaid when there isn't the long-term funding to support them for an appropriate duration or FTE. Institutions and research groups are unwilling to challenge funders on this, leading to cost cutting, impacts on staff mental health, high-turnovers and, ultimately, poorer quality work. In some ways, the fact that this has continued outside of the covid response context makes it even more insidious as it appears to have become the status quo. This does seem to be particularly pronounced in modelling / research intensive organisations and is not something I have noticed since moving to another field. Support staff roles fail to be properly understood within institutions like LSHTM (where I have experience) - or supported to develop. Support staff are burnt out, unsatisfied and under-appreciated. There has been discussion of these issues in relaiton to the COVID-19 inquiry so I am choosing to be optimistic that it will be become more expected that minutes will be published and that a wider range of inputs will be encouraged - for instance there has been discusison and criticism about the lack of remit for economic modelling/joint modelling of epidmeiological and economic modelling within SPI-M-O so hopefully this wil change in future. I think tha individuals are seeking to change this in the research they are putting together now. | | 5|Increase the transparency of the evidence pathway |not sure although in the UK the inquiry suggests a willingness to have transparency. But I don't know of any mechanism in place yet to ensure this happens prospectively. | | 10|Increase the transparency of the evidence pathway |Workshops being organised between academia and civil service | | 11|Increase the transparency of the evidence pathway |I do think there are improvements in data access, if stutteringly so.
